newsitem.title: USA: Hilton buys further interest in four hotels.
newsitem.headline: Hilton buys further interest in four hotels.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp said on Monday it had agreed to increase its ownership in four New York and Washington hotels at a cost of $267 million.
The hotels are the 2,041-room New York Hilton & Towers, the 1,143-room Washington Hilton & Towers, the 543-room Capital Hilton in Washington, and 432-room Rye Town Hilton near New York City.
Hilton, which currently owns 50 percent of each of the properties, said it will buy substantially all of the ownership interests in the four from Prudential Insurance Co of America.

The deal involves Prudential's interests on behalf of its PRISA pension fund, the companies said. PRISA is a $1.9 billion equity real estate portfolio Prudential manages on behalf of 80 pension funds, Prudential said.

In August Hilton agreed to buy most of Prudential's ownership interests in the Chicago Hilton & Towers and the San Francisco Hilton & Towers, while Prudential agreed to buy Hilton's interest in the Miami Airport Hilton.
Both deals have been approved by both companies' boards and are expected to be completed by year-end.
